items.description: Turns the head and looks at you on hearing her name.

howTo.setup: A quiet room and about 10 pea-sized treats from her daily ration. Train before a meal, when she is keen.
steps: When she is not looking at you, say her name once in a happy voice.
The instant she turns her head, say “good” and give the treat within a second.
Wait until she looks away, then repeat. No more than 5 times per session.
Never use her name to scold her or before something she dislikes: her name must always predict good things.
howTo.levelUp: She turns at once 4 times out of 5: practice in the yard, then with a family member walking past, then from a little farther away.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she does not turn, the place is too exciting or you are too far: move closer, go somewhere quieter and try again next session.
howTo.mistakes: Repeating her name over and over, rewarding late, and calling her only to end something fun.

items.description: Finds food by smell: first in plain sight, then hidden in a room, then around the farm.

howTo.setup: 5 treats or kibbles from her ration and a room with no other food in sight. Hold her gently, or ask someone to, while you place the food.
steps: Let her watch you put a treat on the floor a yard away, say “find it” and let her go to eat it.
Repeat with the treat half hidden: behind a chair leg or under the corner of a cloth.
Hide it out of sight in the same room, say “find it” and let her work it out with her nose; praise her calmly when she finds it.
Stop after 3–5 finds, while she still wants more.
howTo.levelUp: She finds it easily 4 times out of 5: hide it in another room, then in the grass of the yard, then around the farm (weeks 2 and 3 of the plan).
howTo.troubleshoot: If she gives up or looks at you, make it easier: put the food back in sight or closer and help her by pointing near it.
howTo.mistakes: Always pointing at the food, hiding it too hard too soon, and long sessions that tire her.

items.description: Sits on the verbal cue or the hand signal.

howTo.setup: Stand in front of her in a quiet place with treats in your hand. Do not say the word yet.
steps: Hold a treat at her nose and move it slowly up and back over her head: her rear will go down on its own.
The moment her rear touches the floor, say “good” and give the treat.
After about 5 good repetitions, make the same movement with an empty hand and reward from the other hand.
When she always sits following your hand, say “sit” just before the gesture.
Release her with “joga” so she knows the exercise is over.
howTo.levelUp: She sits at once 4 times out of 5: say “sit” with a smaller gesture, then in other rooms, then in the yard with few distractions.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she jumps, your hand is too high: keep it right at her nose. If she backs away, practice with a wall behind her.
howTo.mistakes: Pushing her rear down, saying “sit” several times, and rewarding when she is already getting up.

items.description: Comes to you when called. Special reward: boiled chicken.

howTo.setup: Boiled chicken in small pieces, only for this exercise. Start indoors, 1–2 yards from her and, if you can, with a second person.
steps: Crouch down, open your arms and say her name and “come” once, in a happy voice.
Take one or two steps back to invite her to follow you.
When she reaches you, gently hold her collar, say “good” and give her the chicken.
Release her with “joga” so coming to you does not always mean the fun is over.
With two people, call her in turns from different spots in the room.
howTo.levelUp: She comes at once 4 times out of 5: increase the distance, then call her from another room, then in the fenced yard.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she does not come, do not repeat or chase her: run the other way, crouch down or make a funny noise, and make the next call easier and closer.
howTo.mistakes: Calling her for something she dislikes (a bath, being shut in), calling when she surely will not come, and scolding her when she finally arrives.

items.description: Walks next to you on a loose leash.

howTo.setup: A light collar or harness and a 6-foot leash. Start indoors or in the yard, before a walk, with treats in the hand on her side.
steps: Let her wear the collar and leash for a few minutes while she eats or plays, so she gets used to them.
Walk a few steps; every time she is next to your leg with a loose leash, say “good” and give her a treat next to your leg.
If the leash goes tight, stop and stand still; as soon as it loosens, say “good” and keep walking.
Change direction often and reward her when she follows you.
When she walks at your side most of the time, say “heel” just as she reaches your leg, then reward.
howTo.levelUp: 4 out of 5 short walks with a loose leash: walk longer stretches, then in the yard with more smells, then along the farm track.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she pulls all the time, the place is too exciting: go back somewhere quieter and reward more often, every one or two steps.
howTo.mistakes: Pulling the leash back, jerking it, letting her get where she wants by pulling, and walks that are too long for her age.

howTo.setup: Play on the floor with a rope or a soft chew toy at hand. Short games, when she is calm, not when she is overtired.
steps: Play gently with her using your hands and the toy.
If her teeth press hard on your skin, say “ouch” in a soft, high voice and stop the game for a few seconds, hands still.
When she calms down, offer her the toy and keep playing; say “good” if she bites the toy.
If she bites hard again, end the game calmly and leave her a chew toy.
howTo.levelUp: She softens her mouth at once 4 times out of 5: play a little longer and have the rest of the family follow the same rule.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she gets more excited, she is tired or overstimulated: give her a chew toy and let her rest; sleepy puppies bite more.
howTo.mistakes: Pulling your hand away fast (it invites chasing), shouting, tapping her muzzle, and only some people following the rule.

items.description: Lies down following the reward from nose to floor.

howTo.setup: She already sits well. A quiet place, a soft floor or rug and treats in your hand.
steps: Ask her to sit, hold a treat at her nose and lower it slowly straight down to the floor, between her front paws.
Then slide it slowly along the floor away from her: she will stretch out and lie down.
The moment her elbows touch the floor, say “good” and give her the treat on the floor.
After about 5 good repetitions, add the word “down” just before the hand movement.
Release her with “joga”.
howTo.levelUp: She lies down at once 4 times out of 5: use a smaller gesture, then practice in other places with few distractions.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she stands up, move the treat more slowly and closer to her chest; reward halfway (head low) and build up little by little.
howTo.mistakes: Pushing her shoulders down, moving the treat too fast, and asking her to stay down for long at this age.

items.description: Moves away from a closed hand or something on the ground.

howTo.setup: Two kinds of treats: plain ones in a closed hand and better ones in the other hand. Sit on the floor next to her.
steps: Show her your closed hand with a treat inside and let her sniff, lick or paw at it without opening it.
The moment she moves her nose away, say “good” and give her a treat from the other hand, never the one in the closed hand.
Repeat until she moves away quickly; then say “leave it” just as you show the closed hand.
Next, put the treat on the floor under your hand and do the same.
howTo.levelUp: She moves away at once 4 times out of 5: uncover the treat a little, then leave it on the floor in sight, ready to cover it.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she manages to grab it, it was too hard: go back to the closed hand and make the next repetitions easier.
howTo.mistakes: Letting her eat the forbidden treat after leaving it, saying “leave it” over and over, and using it in situations she cannot win yet.

items.description: Holds a sit for a few seconds until released with joga.

howTo.setup: She already sits every time. Stand in front of her in a quiet place with the treats ready.
steps: Ask her to sit, show her your open palm and say “stay” once.
Count one second, say “good” and give her the treat while she is still sitting.
Release her with “joga” and invite her to move.
Add one second at a time: 2, 3, 5 seconds, always rewarding before she gets up.
Later, take one small step back and return to her to reward.
howTo.levelUp: She holds it 4 times out of 5: increase time or distance, never both at once, then add a few distractions.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she gets up before you release her, you asked too much: go back to the last time or distance she managed and build from there.
howTo.mistakes: Calling her to you out of the “stay” (that is another exercise), forgetting the release word, and increasing time and distance together.

items.description: Relieves herself in the usual spot.

howTo.setup: Choose one spot in the yard, always the same. Take her there when she wakes up, after eating, after playing and every 1–2 hours.
steps: Carry her or walk her on the leash straight to the spot, without playing on the way.
Wait quietly; as she starts, say “go potty” in a calm voice.
When she finishes, say “good” and give her a treat right there, within seconds.
Then, as a bonus, a little play or exploring.
howTo.levelUp: She goes in her spot 4 times out of 5: space the outings out a little, as long as there are no accidents.
howTo.troubleshoot: If there is an accident, clean it with an enzymatic cleaner without saying anything and take her out more often; an accident only means she needed to go out sooner.
howTo.mistakes: Scolding accidents (it teaches her to hide), rewarding late once back inside, and changing the spot.
